binders: n is an arbitrary natural number.
fp is an arbitrary floating-addition model. Write u for its real error bound and flAdd for its binary real addition operation.
x and wHat are arbitrary real vectors indexed by Fin n, hence each has exactly n components.
j is an arbitrary element of Fin n.
epsilonExp, epsilonDiv, and deltaDiv are arbitrary real numbers.
hypotheses: For every pair of real operands a and b, there exists a real delta depending on a and b such that |delta| <= u and flAdd(a,b)=(a+b)(1+delta).
For every i in Fin n, 0 <= wHat_i.
For every i in Fin n, |wHat_i-exp(x_i)| <= epsilonExp*exp(x_i).
n*u < 1, where n is viewed as a real number.
eta = epsilonExp + gamma_n(u)*(1+epsilonExp) is strictly less than 1.
conclusions: The scalar componentwise relative error satisfies |pHat_j-p_j|/|p_j| <= (rho+eta)/(1-eta), where pHat_j, p_j, rho, and eta are defined below.
mathematical_definitions: Fin n is the index set {0,...,n-1}.
gamma_n(u) = n*u/(1-n*u), with n embedded in the reals.
S = sum over i in Fin n of exp(x_i).

Define flSum_0(v)=0. For a one-element vector, flSum_1(v)=v_0. For k >= 1, flSum_(k+1)(v)=flAdd(flSum_k(i maps to v_i for i<k),v_k). Thus entries are accumulated from left to right in increasing index order.
Every occurrence of |.| is the ordinary scalar absolute value on the reals, not a vector norm.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every dimension n, every modeled floating-point addition operation with unit bound u, every real vectors x and wHat of length n, every component j, and every real error parameters epsilonExp, epsilonDiv, and deltaDiv satisfying the listed assumptions, compare the exact normalized exponential p_j=exp(x_j)/sum_i exp(x_i) with pHat_j obtained by dividing wHat_j by the left-to-right floating-point sum of wHat and multiplying by 1+deltaDiv. If n*u<1 and eta=epsilonExp+[n*u/(1-n*u)](1+epsilonExp)<1, then their scalar relative error is at most (epsilonExp+epsilonDiv+epsilonExp*epsilonDiv+eta)/(1-eta).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: When n=0, Fin n has no element j, so the universally quantified assertion is vacuous for that dimension.
In every nonvacuous case, the existence of j implies n>=1. Together with 0<=u and n*u<1 this gives u<1.
The hypotheses n*u<1, eta<1, and epsilonExp>=0 imply epsilonExp<1. Consequently every wHat_i is strictly positive in a nonempty dimension, because exp(x_i)>0 and its relative error is below 1.

For nonempty dimensions, the exact exponential sum is positive. The modeled addition rule, u<1, and positivity of the entries also make the recursively computed sum positive. Thus the normalization denominators and p_j are nonzero, although nonzeroness is not stated as a separate hypothesis.
The denominator 1-eta on the right is positive because eta<1.
There is no smallness assumption on epsilonDiv; only epsilonDiv>=0 and |deltaDiv|<=epsilonDiv are required.
wHat and deltaDiv are arbitrary supplied quantities satisfying inequalities. The proposition does not assert that a particular implementation generated them.
The local addition-error witness may depend independently on each pair of operands. No single common delta is required for all additions.
The computed sum has a fixed left-to-right index order. No associativity, commutativity, or right-zero identity is assumed for flAdd.
For n=1, the computed sum is exactly wHat_0 and performs no call to flAdd.

Only the additions used in the denominator are governed by fp's error model. The proposition does not separately model rounding of exponential evaluation, multiplication, or division beyond epsilonExp and the supplied factor 1+deltaDiv.

The conclusion is a bound for one scalar normalized component at a time, universally over j; it does not state a vector-norm error bound, tightness, probabilistic behavior, or an algorithmic implementation theorem.
